rationale:
Changed: folded in the course elevation you provided today (the clubmate's file that also mapped Cheltenham) for the Sharpness 4 entry on 4 Oct. Two things move. First, the projection: the 27 Sep version said 'realistically inside 23:39, coin-flip against 23:30' off flat Riegel numbers alone. Her ~23:40 on this course — run at near-identical half-marathon form to you (1:21:02 to your 1:21:03) — came in ~38 sec slower than a flat Riegel off her time predicts, so the honest band is now 23:35-23:55: the record is possible on a good day, more likely just outside, and a coin flip at best against the top of the range rather than the middle. That's a genuine downgrade and it's said plainly in the notes below, not softened. Second, the pacing note stops being generic ('hold effort on the climbs') and becomes the actual shape of the course — downhill trap at km 1, climb to 2 km, a drag from 3-4.3 km, the crux at km 6 (two steep ramps, her slowest split), downhill to the line — so effort management has something concrete to work from instead of just 'it's lumpy.' Fixtures.json already carries this detail from the same source; the race entry below now matches it rather than lagging behind it with the vaguer 27 Sep version.

One thing this doesn't change: Tuesday's 6x200m target (3:38-3:40/km). That's a flat-effort neuromuscular opener, not a rehearsal of race pacing, so the course profile has nothing to say about it — it stays as written.

Worth carrying the same caveat fixtures.json carries: when she ran it and at what fitness isn't known, so her time is a calibration point, not a guarantee — treat 23:35-23:55 as the honest planning band, not a hard boundary either way.

Everything else stands exactly as proposed on the 27th, because nothing else in your message touches it: the recovery week came through clean (achilles 0 every day, physio-flagged tightness resolved by Thursday, HRV/RHR back to normal, ACWR OPTIMAL/LOW throughout) — the trigger the last review named for resuming something sharper than pure easy running, short of the full Saturday/Wednesday spine because a hard session the day before a race is never right. Rebuild volume, one light neuromuscular touch Tuesday, strides Friday, easy shakeout Saturday. The four-week Guy Fawkes sharpening block still gets written next Sunday once this race is done, not guessed at today.

changes.notes: Rest - normal week rhythm resuming. Recovery week complete: achilles 0 every day, the physio-flagged tightness resolved, HRV and RHR back to normal range. Clean to build back up.
Easy 8km, conversational - continuing the rebuild toward norm volume.

First bit of speed since Cheltenham, deliberately light: 3km warm-up, 6x200m at ~4-mile effort (3:38-3:40/km) with FULL recovery between reps - jog/walk until actually recovered, not a fixed short rest, so every rep is fresh rather than accumulating fatigue - 3km cool-down. ~9-10km all in. This is a neuromuscular touch, not a return to the Saturday/Wednesday quality spine - that waits for the actual sharpening block once Sunday's race outcome is known.
Easy 6km. If a leg gym session is due this week, this is the point to have already had it - keep any heavy lower-body work at least 72h clear of Sunday, whichever race it turns out to be.
Easy 5km + 4-6 strides. Legs sharp for Sunday, not tired - strides stay controlled, not a speed session.
Easy 30-35 min shakeout, conversational throughout, no strides. The day before a race - whichever one it turns out to be - stays easy regardless.

CONFIRMED: club 4-mile road race (the Sharpness 4), Crete is off. Club record reads '23:3' on the list, so 23:30-23:39 (3:39/km average for 23:30, 3:40/km for 23:39). COURSE (elevation from a clubmate's file - the same clubmate whose 1:21:02 Cheltenham run mapped that course): rolling, ~51m of climbing on her watch, no barometric altimeter so treat the metres as approximate and the shape as the signal. Km 1 is downhill then flat - her fastest full km of the race (3:32) - the same trap as Cheltenham's km 1, do not copy it, go out closer to 3:38. First climb to ~2km (+13m). Km 3 drops then starts rising. A long drag from 3km to ~4.3km. Km 5 dips. The crux is km 6: two short steep ramps around 5.1-5.7km, her slowest split by ten seconds - expect that to be the slowest km of the race and do not chase it back. Downhill last ~0.4km to the line. Run it on effort, not pace: let the climbs cost a few seconds, take the descents, use the downhill finish. HER TIME (~23:40) IS THE REAL CALIBRATION, not the flat Riegel numbers: she ran 1:21:02 at Cheltenham against his 1:21:03 - near-identical half-marathon form - and went ~38 sec slower on this course than a flat Riegel off that time predicts. Stacked against him too: two weeks without quality since a maximal half. Honest read: roughly 23:35-23:55 - the record is possible on a good day, more likely just outside, and a coin flip at best against the top of that range, not the confident 'inside 23:39' read from before this course data came in. Caveat: when she ran it and at what fitness isn't known, so treat her time as calibration, not gospel. There's a team prize on the line too, which he'd like to help with - doesn't change the individual prescription, he's already racing this flat out rather than treating it as a jog. Full protocol: Symbicort 20 min / salbutamol 15 min before gun, Puma Fast-R Nitro 3, proper 3km warm-up. Afterwards: 2-3 easy days into the Guy Fawkes block, no recovery week needed for a 4-mile.
